descriptionChirho: To clasp someone in one's arms as a greeting, expression of affection, or reunion, used in both Piel intensive and Qal stems with consistent multilingual translation evidence (abrazar, गले लगाना, عانق, 껴안다, kukumbatia).

To fold or cross one's hands idly, as in the proverbial image of laziness ('a little folding of the hands to sleep'), with distinctly different translation vocabulary across languages (folding, cruza, बाँधता, يَطْوِي, anakunjia).
